evals.prompt: My mom has dementia and keeps asking where her mother is, but her mother has been gone for 20 years. Every time I remind her, she gets upset all over again. I don't know if I should keep correcting her.
evals.expected_output: Recommends validation-therapy approach (respond to the underlying emotion rather than correcting the fact), explains why repeated correction causes repeated grief, and gives a concrete alternative phrasing to try.

evals.prompt: I have ADHD and I own like four planners but I never actually check any of them. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Reframes this as an externalization/point-of-performance problem rather than a discipline failure, suggests concrete techniques (reminders placed where the action happens, visual timers, body doubling) instead of 'just use a planner more consistently'.

evals.prompt: My dad with Alzheimer's wandered out of the house last week and we found him three blocks away. We're scared to death. What should we actually do?
evals.expected_output: Addresses immediate safety (wearable ID linked to an emergency response service, door alarms/sensors) and acknowledges caregiver fear, without suggesting medication changes directly.
